plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Bidding higher than my value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth if others bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to inform deviation, I'll bid exactly my value of $31.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid rather than my own bid, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > others' bids) and never overpay (I never pay more than my value). Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid between my true value and my inflated bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, truthful bidding at $37 is optimal.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value risks negative profit, and bidding below reduces my chance of winning without improving the price I'd pay. With no prior round history to adjust for opponent tendencies, the optimal and risk-free strategy is to bid exactly my value of $11.
